column1: # - NativeBoundary runtime requirements for Rust-backed std APIs.
# - Assigns every Rust-backed std operation a capability, blocking policy,
#   cancellation policy, timeout policy, worker placement, resource policy, and
#   typed-error policy before the operation can cross the NativeBoundary.

column9: notes
Package-owned host clock observations return copied integers without retaining resources; observations are effectful and never cacheable.
Ed25519 verification is a bounded pure-value transformation over admitted payload text and never exposes key material or native resources.
SHA-256 byte and framed-field operations are bounded value transformations and return VM-owned digest text.
Serde JSON value operations do not carry native resources.
TOML parsing produces an existing VM-owned JSON value and carries no parser or host resource.
Base64 operations are bounded value transformations.
MD5 digest operations are bounded compatibility transformations and must not be treated as secure hashing.
Path APIs transform path values and do not open files.
URI APIs parse and inspect value data only.
Registry publication parsing applies the compiler-owned strict protocol model and shared bounded admission policy, returning only VM-owned primitive metadata.
Random APIs use maintained Rust RNG crates and return explicit VM-owned generator state.
Regex APIs use the maintained Rust regex engine and return opaque VM-owned regex values.
Argument inspection reads immutable process-start metadata and returns VM-owned values.
Environment and current-directory inspection perform bounded host metadata reads and return VM-owned values.
Platform current reads immutable target constants; dynamic metrics use a separate VM-owned capability transition.
Request inspection is value based.
Cookie APIs construct and inspect typed header values.
Response APIs construct typed response values.
Session APIs operate on VM-owned session handles and typed cookie metadata.
Package-owned maintained SSE codec encodes copied event values; response composition executes in Terlan and uses no host executor.
TLS APIs construct typed configuration; certificate and ACME host work requires asynchronous capability handoff.
Postgres operations use worker-owned pool and connection resources.
Vector handles are VM-tracked native resources with stale-handle checks.
Cluster descriptors and bounded session state are actor-owned; these operations do not launch workers or perform network I/O.
Conflict, version, store, and snapshot operations use an owner-checked VM resource registry without host persistence.

Local descriptors and checkpoints remain actor-owned; durable operations require an explicitly bound sandboxed storage worker, bounded deadlines, and asynchronous completion. Cancellation does not imply rollback of an unacknowledged mutation.
Fault monitors and recovery descriptors are owner-checked logical state; observation uses supplied ticks and performs no host timer or network work.
Scheduling plans and migration descriptors are actor-owned logical state; these operations do not launch processes or execute remote migrations.
The internal libpq driver uses worker-owned connection resources and typed failures.
